title: Pass a tray of filled espresso cups from one hand to the other across a serving gap, level
instruction: Move the white tray of blue cups from the grey pad on the left to the grey pad on the right and set it down level, with no cup tipped. Neither arm reaches both pads; do not put the tray down in between.
context: Done by: waiters and waitresses (O*NET 35-3031, about 2 million workers in the US) and food servers (35-3023) carry trays of filled cups and regularly pass a tray from one hand to the other in mid-air to reach a far counter; a tilted tray spills the drinks. Here the two serving counters are 0.80 m apart, farther than either arm reaches, so the tray must change hands in the air and be set down level on the far counter. Unlike the board's single-hand tray tasks, the tray here must change hands in mid-air. Cups are small espresso/sample cups on a small tray, not full-size drinks, because of the simulated grip strength (see fidelity).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Left pad: grey 13 x 34 cm, 3 mm thick, centre x 30, y +40. Right pad: same, centre x 30, y -40. Rack: white plate 9 x 23 cm, 12 mm thick, 150 g, friction 0.6, with an upright handle block 6 x 4 x 4 cm at each short end (handle centres y +-13.5 from the plate centre) and three 6 mm high shallow wells. It starts centred on the left pad. Three blue cups (4.5 cm diameter, 6 cm tall, 30 g each including 30 mL of water, friction 0.8) stand in the wells at y -5.5, 0, +5.5 from the plate centre.
scoring: Zero (latched) if a cup spills (tilted over 20 degrees or off the plate), the rack tilts over 20 degrees while carried, or the rack is left on the table away from both pads. 0.25: the left arm holds the rack (gripper at a handle, fingers closed on it), lifts it at least 4 cm and carries it past y = +15 cm with the cups upright. 0.5: verified in-air transfer, in order: left arm holds it, then right arm holds it, then the left arm has let go while the right still holds it, with the rack at least 20 mm above the pad throughout (if the rack touches a pad in between, the chain restarts) and carry tilt never above 8 degrees. 0.75: then the rack plate rests on the right pad, its underside within 3 mm of the pad top, within 15 mm of the pad centre, within 8 degrees of yaw and under 4 degrees of tilt. 1.0: additionally all three cups within 15 mm of their wells, the rack still, both arms still and both grippers open and off the handles, all true for 20 consecutive steps (1 s). The score stays at 0.75 until that hold completes; 0.75 and 1.0 are judged on the current state, so they drop if the rack is later lifted or moved off the pad.
reset_notes: Stand the cups in the wells on the plate, set the rack centred on the left pad with its long side along y.
fidelity: Real vs simulated: real drinking cups are about 75 x 95 mm, 150-200 mL of water, about 0.2 kg each on a 0.6-1 kg serving tray; here cups are espresso size (45 x 60 mm, solid cylinders, 0.03 kg each, 30 mL of water lumped in) on a 0.15 kg rack, because the simulated pinch grip could not lift the real-size load (tried: demo scored 0). No liquid is simulated; a spill is a cup tilted over 20 degrees or off the plate. Scoring reads object poses and the two gripper links (finger gap, TCP) from the simulator; the demo reads only its own joint positions.
